clue.text: Beau offers diamonds, perhaps, and gold

parts.note: diamonds are one suit in a pack of cards; 'perhaps' marks it as an example
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A boyfriend shows his devotion with gifts of jewels and gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamonds' looks like jewellery but it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is an old-fashioned word for a man courting a woman, a wooer.

clue.text: Demonstrator gets over the top in tall building

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes in the synonym for demonstrator

parts.note: a shower is one who shows or demonstrates

explanation.surface: A protester goes over the top in a tall building, clambering too high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstrator' suggests a protester; here it is someone who shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot tower is a tall tower where molten lead was dropped to form shot, a tall structure.

clue.text: Finds emails oddly lacking perfection

indicators.note: lacking the odd-numbered letters, keeping only the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone notices emails missing in a strange way, hardly perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a model of perfection, a standard of excellence.

clue.text: Away team's kit is best

parts.note: someone away is out
a sports team's kit is its strip

explanation.surface: A football fan rates the away kit as the team's finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip is to surpass, as to best an opponent is to defeat them.

clue.text: Be stuck with headache, having little energy for celebration

parts.note: to jam is to become stuck fast
a headache, in the sense of a tiresome nuisance, is a bore

indicators.note: a little of the word energy is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone stuck with a headache and low on energy is in no mood to party.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large, lively gathering or party, so it is a kind of festivity.

clue.text: Outrageous male wearing brogues and dress?

indicators.note: the regional speech wears, so contains, the other pieces

parts.note: a brogue is a regional, especially Irish, accent
outre means unconventional or outrageous

explanation.surface: An outlandish man sports brogue shoes with a dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brogues' look like shoes but are accents of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Accoutrements are items of clothing and equipment, so dress in a broad sense; the question mark flags the looseness.

clue.text: Government department said bank supports leading pair in business

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits beneath
the leading pair are the first two letters of the word
said means the word is spoken and its sound used

parts.note: a bank of seats is a row

explanation.surface: A ministry promises a bank will back the business leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is an office or agency of government, such as the US Federal Bureau of Investigation.

clue.text: Church inspector finally coming over to assess cleric's office

indicators.note: coming over means turned over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to rate something is to assess it

explanation.surface: A church inspector arrives at last to evaluate a vicar's position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming over' reverses CE plus R to give REC.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectorate is the office or term held by a rector, a parish priest.

clue.text: Announced openers for South Africa test

indicators.note: something announced is spoken, so the sound of the letters counts

parts.note: the first letters of the two words are S and A

explanation.surface: The opening batsmen for South Africa are named for a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: S and A spoken as letter names give 'ess-ay'. 'Test' and 'openers' suggest cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt or trial, so to essay something is to test it.

clue.text: Except for beginning, upright piano accompanies English dance

indicators.note: piano accompanies, so goes along with and follows, the English abbreviation
everything except the opening letter is kept, so the first letter of the synonym goes

parts.note: an upright person is honest
p is the musical marking for piano, softly

explanation.surface: An upright piano provides the music for an English dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright piano' reads as one instrument, but 'upright' means honest and 'piano' gives P.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-step is a ballroom dance of the early twentieth century, done with one step per beat.

clue.text: Fellow will initially act drunk and create mayhem

indicators.note: these two pieces come initially, before the fellow's words

parts.note: to play a part is to act
merry is a mild word for tipsy or drunk
a fellow is a he
'll is the contracted form of will

explanation.surface: A man warns he will get drunk and run riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but it only says the acting and drinking come before the fellow's contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means cause a great deal of trouble or chaos.

clue.text: Remains briefly to tour area in capital

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the shortened word surrounds the abbreviation
a word cut briefly loses its final letter

parts.note: a carcass is the remains of a dead animal

explanation.surface: Remains are being taken around some area of a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims CARCASS to CARCAS before A goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Caracas is the capital city of Venezuela.

clue.text: I'll leave room of house available for rent

indicators.note: the letter I will leave the word, so it is taken out

parts.note: a toilet is a room in a house

explanation.surface: A lodger announces they are moving out, so a room in the house is up for rent.
explanation.walkthrough: The I of 'I'll' is the letter removed; the 'll' is just future tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign reading 'to let' says a property can be rented by a tenant.

clue.text: Praising a politician after introduction of bill — extremely unusual

indicators.note: a Tory comes after the opening pieces, which introduce him

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a bill posted up

indicators.note: the extreme letters of a word are its first and last

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone praises a politician once an extremely unusual bill has been introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduction of bill' suggests taking a first letter, but 'introduction of' is a position signal: the bill and the extremes go in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulatory describes fawning, flattering admiration, so it is a synonym of flattering.

clue.text: Mother was struggling to carry one in addition to that

indicators.note: the jumbled letters carry, that is hold, the numeral inside
struggling letters are thrown into disorder, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A mother was struggling to carry a single child or bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning furthermore or besides, adding a point.

clue.text: People with degrees employed in reform school

indicators.note: employed in means put to work inside, so placed within

parts.note: to alter is to change or reform
an MA is a Master of Arts, so two of them are people with degrees

explanation.surface: Graduates find work in a reform school.
explanation.definitionFit: One's alma mater is the school or university one attended.

clue.text: Arms deployed to get spoils

indicators.note: troops deployed are rearranged into position, so the letters move

explanation.surface: Weapons are put into action to seize plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to damage or ruin it, so the verb is a synonym of spoils.

clue.text: Twitter revealed I'm not married

definitions.note: spoken by the unmarried person, so stands for a noun describing them

parts.note: birds twitter, so twittering is a kind of singing
to let on is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: Someone announces on social media that they are unattached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twitter' suggests the social network but is the verb for birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is an unattached, unwed person, who might declare themselves so.

clue.text: Dept's reorganised: have to resign

indicators.note: reorganised letters are put into a new order

parts.note: to own is to have

explanation.surface: After a department shake-up, an official is obliged to quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To step down is to stand down from a post, leaving it voluntarily.

clue.text: Light-hearted film, perhaps, from Pasolini, cut

indicators.note: the answer is a piece cut out of the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: A cheerful scene has been edited out of a Pasolini picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Pier Paolo Pasolini was an Italian film director, so 'from Pasolini, cut' reads like editing.
explanation.definitionFit: A romp is a lively, light comedy, and a film is one example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Expert with plan taking in the Titanic?

parts.note: a pro is an expert

indicators.note: the second synonym takes the other word into its middle

parts.note: to mean to do something is to plan it

explanation.surface: An expert with a scheme for the Titanic, the doomed liner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titanic' suggests the ship, but here it means belonging to the Titans of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Prometheus was a Titan, so anything Promethean is literally Titanic, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A Liberal proved untrustworthy in coalition

parts.note: someone who lied proved they could not be trusted

explanation.surface: A Liberal partner in a coalition government broke their promises.
explanation.definitionFit: Allied means joined in an alliance, united with partners.

clue.text: Half of hits by guy, including a song from a vast range

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters
the synonym for man includes, so holds, the other pieces

parts.note: a guy is a man
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A singer covers half his hits and a song drawn from a huge repertoire.
explanation.definitionFit: Himalayan describes what comes from the Himalayas, the vast mountain range.

clue.text: Clubs out of liquor? That leads to a commotion

indicators.note: the letter is out of, so missing from, the word

parts.note: hooch is cheap or illicit liquor
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A bar runs out of drink, and a brawl breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' suggests nightclubs; here it is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is a fuss or uproar, a noisy stir.

clue.text: Boy keeled over on exercise bike

indicators.note: in a down or across charade, on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: PE stands for physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: a boat that has keeled over is upside down, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy collapsed while working out on an exercise bike.
explanation.definitionFit: To bike is to cycle, which is done by pushing the pedals, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Drive solo aircraft

parts.note: Dr is the street-name abbreviation for Drive
solo means alone, one

explanation.surface: An instruction to pilot a plane single-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is an unmanned flying machine, controlled remotely.

clue.text: Jumbo published by setter for paper?

parts.note: a book that is out has been published
size is a gluey wash used to stiffen and seal paper, so it sets paper

explanation.surface: A giant puzzle produced by a newspaper's crossword setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler but is the glaze applied to paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo means extra large, the same as an oversized garment or item.

clue.text: Night owl determined to secure work

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: stout means resolute or determined
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A resolute night owl is determined to find a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop-out is someone who stays out late at night, a night owl in its social sense.

clue.text: Dog given outing needs drink

parts.note: a thing aired has been given an outing, put on show
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: A dog taken for a walk comes back thirsty.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire, so a breed of dog.

clue.text: Student days in college ultimately spent in pub

indicators.note: the shortened word goes in the synonym for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: the ultimate, final letter is spent, so used up and gone

parts.note: a term is a period of days in college

explanation.surface: A student's college days end up being spent drinking in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately spent' drops the last letter of TERM, leaving TER.
explanation.definitionFit: An intern is a trainee, especially a medical graduate still learning on the job.
